title: Germany – Public-service buses – Beschaffung, Wartung und Reparatur von Wasserstoffhybrid- und batterieelektrischen Bussen für den ÖPNV
description: Die Regionalverkehr Köln GmbH (RVK) ist ein modernes Verkehrsunternehmen, das die Kapazität, das Wissen und das verbindliche Ziel hat, die Menschen im Rheinland auf technisch höchstem Niveau zu bewegen. Zusammen mit ihren Eigentümern und Auftraggebern arbeitet die RVK stetig an der Umsetzung eines attraktiven, umweltschonenden und nachhaltigen Nahverkehrs. Mehr als 1.050 Konzernmitarbeiterinnen und -mitarbeiter sorgen dafür, dass jährlich mehr als 23 Millionen Fahrgäste sicher zum Ziel kommen. Das Kern-Verkehrsgebiet der RVK erstreckt sich über den Kreis Euskirchen, den Rheinisch-Bergischen Kreis und den linksrheinischen Rhein-Sieg-Kreis. Daneben erbringt die RVK ihre Leistungen auch in den Städten Köln, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl und Wesseling. Die Leistungserstellung erfolgt sowohl auf eigenen Linien als auch im Auftrag anderer Verkehrsunternehmen. Gegenstand des Vergabeverfahrens ist die Beschaffung, Wartung und Reparatur von Wasserstoffhybrid- und batterieelektrischen Solobussen für den öffentlichen Personennahverkehr. Der Beschaffungszeitraum erstreckt sich über die Jahre 2027 bis 2029. Die Vergabe erfolgt in zwei Losen: Los 1 – Wasserstoffhybrid-Solobusse Beschaffung von 8 Wasserstoffhybrid-Solobussen als verbindliche Abnahmemenge sowie optional bis zu 29 weiteren Fahrzeugen einschließlich der zugehörigen Wartungs- und Reparaturleistungen; Höchstmenge sind 37 Fahrzeuge. Los 2 – Batterieelektrische Solobusse Beschaffung von 49 batterieelektrischen Solobussen als verbindliche Abnahmemenge sowie optional bis zu 19 weiteren Fahrzeugen einschließlich der zugehörigen Wartungs- und Reparaturleistungen. Höchstmenge sind 68 Fahrzeuge. Ebenfalls Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen ist die Wartung und Instandhaltung der Fahrzeuge im Rahmen eines Full-Service-Vertrages über die Lebensdauer der Fahrzeuge (12 Jahre). Die Vergabeunterlagen werden insoweit vorsehen, dass spätestens mit dem verbindlichen Angebot ein geeignetes Werkstättennetz nachzuweisen ist. Einzelheiten ergeben sich aus den Vergabeunterlagen. Die vorliegende Beschaffung steht aufgrund von der Auftraggeberin nicht allein beeinflussbarer Umstände in folgender Hinsicht unter Aufhebungsvorbehalten: Zur Umsetzung des Projekts ist die Auftraggeberin zwingend auf die Gewährung öffentlicher Fördermittel angewiesen. Diese sind beantragt; ein Förderbescheid wurde indes bis dato noch nicht erlassen, soll jedoch bis zur Auftragserteilung gesichert werden. Wenn nicht vor Zuschlag eine Förderung erfolgt, die die Kosten des Projekts nachhaltig abdeckt, behält sich der AG vor, das Verfahren (ggf. auch bezogen auf ein einzelnes Los) aufzuheben und keinen Zuschlag zu erteilen.

title: Germany – Financial auditing services – Rahmenvereinbarung über Jahresabschlussprüfungen für die Geschäftsjahre 2027 bis 2031
description: Die Duisburger Hafen AG (duisport) ist die Eigentums- und Managementgesellschaft des Duisburger Hafens, des größten Binnenhafens der Welt. Ideale Standortbedingungen, eine einzigartige geographische Lage und umfassendes Logistik-Know-how machen den Hafen als trimodale Logistikdrehscheibe zu einem der wichtigsten Dreh- und Angelpunkte für den Warenverkehr in Europa. Das Netzwerk aus Industrie- und Logistikwirtschaft spielt eine zentrale Rolle beim Aufbau und bei der Optimierung nationaler und internationaler Lieferketten. Durch die multimodale Verknüpfung internationaler Warenströme hat der Duisburger Hafen eine Schlüsselrolle und fungiert als Tor zu den europäischen Märkten. Das Dienstleistungsangebot der duisport-Gruppe unterteilt sich in drei Geschäftsbereiche: Infra- und Suprastruktur, Verkehr und logistische Dienstleistungen sowie Industrielogistik. Die NRW.HOLDING GmbH (Düsseldorf) hält zwei Drittel der Anteile an der Duisburger Hafen AG. Ein Drittel der Anteile hält die Stadt Duisburg. Gegenstand des Vergabeverfahrens ist der Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung über Prüfungsleistungen für den Zeitraum der Geschäftsjahre 2027 bis 2031. Ein Anspruch auf Abruf von Einzelaufträgen besteht nicht. Die später auf Grundlage der Rahmenvereinbarung jährlich erteilten Prüfungsaufträge umfassen die Prüfung und Testierung des Einzel- und Konzernabschlusses der Duisburger Hafen AG sowie diverser Tochtergesellschaften und Beteiligungen (3 große, 3 mittelgroße, 9 kleine Kapitalgesellschaften und 6 Kleinstkapitalgesellschaften) sowie 1 mittelgroße und 1 kleine GmbH & Co. KG jeweils nach HGB durch einen Wirtschaftsprüfer bzw. eine Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft. Es gilt zu berücksichtigen, dass mit Ausnahme von zwei Gesellschaften alle Gesellschaften ihre Abschlüsse nach den Vorschriften für große Kapitalgesellschaften aufstellen. Der Prüfungsumfang umfasst zwingend alle zur ordnungsgemäßen Jahresabschlussprüfung gehörenden Prüfungshandlungen einschließlich der Prüfung nach § 53 HGrG. Hinzu kommen: • betriebswirtschaftliche Prüfung der Bezüge der Mitglieder des Vorstands sowie der leitenden Angestellten • Prüfung des Tantiemeberichts für die Mitglieder des Vorstands • Prüfung des Berichtes des Vorstandes über Beziehungen zu verbundenen Unternehmen (Abhängigkeitsbericht) • Prüfung der Einhaltung des Public Corporate Governance Kodexes des Landes NRW für die duisport-Gruppe und die voll konsolidierten Gesellschaften des Konzerns • Separate Prüfung nach § 53 HGrG sowie Prüfung der Einhaltung des Public Corporate Governance Kodexes des Landes NRW für eine Beteiligungsgesellschaft • Separate Prüfung nach § 53 HGrG sowie Prüfung der Einhaltung des Public Corporate Governance Kodexes der Stadt Duisburg für eine Tochter- und für eine Beteiligungsgesellschaft • Vom Aufsichtsrat vorgegebene Prüfungsschwerpunkte - 3-4 Schwerpunkte p.a. aus dem Bereich Buchhaltungs- und Businessprozesse - 1 Schwerpunkt p.a. aus dem Bereich Compliance-Managementsystem mit separater Berichterstattung Die Bilanzsumme des Konzerns belief sich zum 31.12.2025 auf 582 Mio. EUR. Das Umsatzvolumen des Geschäftsjahres 2025 lag bei 281 Mio. EUR. Die Anlagenintensität im Konzern betrug zum Stichtag rd. 82%. Die Buchhaltung der deutschen Gesellschaften erfolgt durch die Hauptverwaltung am Standort Duisburg unter Verwendung von Dynamics 365 Business Central. Die Buchhaltung sowie die Jahresabschlusserstellung für die Tochtergesellschaften in der Volksrepublik China, Indien und Polen werden durch externe Dienstleister in den Ländern vor Ort vorgenommen, somit sind die Prüfungen der ausländischen Gesellschaften vor Ort in den jeweiligen Ländern durchzuführen. Die Prüfungshandlungen und Prüfungsfeststellungen sind in einem Abschlussgespräch zu erläutern. Zudem sind für alle geprüften Gesellschaften Prüfungsberichte anzufertigen. Hierbei sind neben den gebundenen Print-Versionen von Prüfungsberichten und Testatsexemplaren auch jeweils elektronische Versionen zur Verfügung zu stellen. Die Prüfungsberichte zum Konzern und zum Einzelabschluss der Duisburger Hafen AG haben zudem Erläuterungen zur Vermögens-, Finanz- und Ertragslage zu beinhalten.

Purpose and Background DLA Energy is conducting market research to identify qualified, capable, and interested commercial sources able to furnish, transport, and deliver recurring bulk quantities of conforming diesel fuel products in support of U.S. Army and USCENTCOM forces operations at Logistics Support Area (LSA) Jenkins & Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB), in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA). Site Operational and Receiving Context: Storage Configuration: LSA Jenkins currently maintains on-site bulk fuel storage consisting of two (2) 50,000 U.S. Gallon (USG) fuel bladders (bags) fully installed and ready to receive product (total capacity: 100,000 USG). Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB) currently maintains a combination of 50,000-gallon bladders, 10,000-gallon bladders, and above-ground storage tanks. Government Receiving Equipment: No additional government-furnished receiving equipment is required or provided; commercial delivery tankers must be fully capable of self-sufficient offloading into bladder and / storage tanks. Operational Scope: Commercial suppliers must demonstrate the capability to source, transport, and offload conforming fuel directly into the government storage bladders while complying strictly with host nation (KSA) laws, environmental standards, safety mandates, and military installation access protocols. 3. Scope of Requirement, Specifications, and Delivery Schedule The Government is seeking sources capable of furnishing Diesel Fuel #2 (DF-2) (Commercial / ASTM D975 or military equivalent), authorized DoD alternative products such as Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel (DS2) (NSN: 9140-01-524-0139), and/or Regular Unleaded Gasoline (MUR) (NSN: 9130-00-148-7103; Commercial Unleaded / ASTM D4814 or military equivalent) meeting all applicable military or recognized commercial/ASTM specifications. Fuel Specifications and Estimated Demand Schedule All quantities and dates are planning estimates and are subject to change in any potential future solicitation. Fuel Type / Nomenclature National Stock Number (NSN) Specification / Standard Delivery Location Estimated Annual Requirement Diesel Fuel #2 (DF-2)(Primary) 9140-00-286-5294 Commercial / ASTM D975 / Military Equivalent LSA Jenkins, KSA 480,000 USG Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel (DS2)(Authorized Alt) 9140-01-524-0139 ULSD (DS2) DoD Alternative Spec LSA Jenkins, KSA 480,000 USG Diesel Fuel, 10 PPM Sulfur (SFD)(Alt) 9140-01-556-9156 SFD (10 PPM max sulfur) LSA Jenkins, KSA 480,000 USG Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel (DS2) 9140-01-524-0139 ULSD (DS2) DoD Alternative Spec PSAB (Al Kharj), KSA 1,080,000 USG Regular Unleaded Gasoline (MUR) 9130-00-148-7103 Commercial Unleaded Gasoline / ASTM D4814 PSAB (Al Kharj), KSA 720,000 USG Logistics Support Area (LSA) Jenkins: Estimated Delivery Frequency: Bi-weekly delivery schedule (two 20,000 USG deliveries per month) to sustain the steady-state 40,000 USG monthly requirement. Total Estimated Annual Program Requirement: 480,000 USG. Estimated Period of Requirement: 1 December 2026 through 30 September 2027 (annual operational baseline). Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB): Estimated Delivery Frequency: DS2: 2 to 3 deliveries per week. MUR: 1 to 2 deliveries per week. Total Estimated Annual Program Requirement: 1,800,000 USG combined (1,080,000 USG DS2 / 720,000 USG MUR) Estimated Period of Requirement: Beginning 1 December 2026. 4. Delivery Location, Site Access, and Delivery Equipment Mode Logistics Support Area (LSA) Jenkins, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Delivery Location: Logistics Support Area (LSA) Jenkins, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Tactical GPS Coordinates: 24.2210435� N, 38.2568021� E Authorized Delivery Days and Hours: Days: Monday through Friday. Weekend Delivery Window: 0800 � 1600 hours (when authorized/coordinated). Holidays: Subject to base operating status during U.S. Federal and host nation (KSA) holidays. Required Mode of Delivery (MoD): Tank Truck with Pump and Meter (TTWP): Commercial delivery vehicles must be tank trucks equipped with operable onboard discharge pumps, calibrated fuel meters, and metered delivery ticket capability. Vendor tankers must carry adequate hose lengths (minimum 50�100 ft) and standard military-compatible camlock/dry-break adapters to connect directly to the 50,000-USG fuel bladders. Base Security, Entry Control Point (ECP), and Escort Protocols: ECP Processing: All commercial delivery trucks and drivers must enter through the designated installation Entry Control Point (ECP) for comprehensive security inspection and credential verification prior to base access. Mandatory Escort: Commercial drivers must remain with and follow designated military/government escorts from the ECP to the fuel discharge point at all times while on the installation. Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB), Al Kharj, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Delivery Location: Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB), Al Kharj, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Authorized Delivery Days and Hours: Days: Monday through Friday (deliveries coordinated in accordance with multiple-weekly demand schedules). Weekend/After-Hours Delivery Window: Coordinated on an as-needed basis with the Base Contracting and Operations teams. Holidays: Subject to base operating status during U.S. Federal and host nation (KSA) holidays. Required Mode of Delivery (MoD): Tank Truck with Pump and Meter (TTWP): Commercial delivery vehicles must be tank trucks equipped with operable onboard discharge pumps, calibrated fuel meters, and metered delivery ticket capability. Vendor tankers must carry adequate hose lengths and standard military-compatible adapters to connect directly to the mix of 50,000-gallon and 10,000-gallon bladders and above-ground storage tanks on-site. Base Security, Entry Control Point (ECP), and Escort Protocols: Host Nation Plate Restriction: All commercial delivery vehicles seeking entry to Prince Sultan Air Base must be equipped with valid Saudi Arabian license plates. ECP Processing: Delivery trucks and operators must enter through the designated PSAB Entry Control Point (ECP) for technical safety inspections, cargo checks, and driver credential verification. Mandatory Escort: Commercial drivers must be met at the ECP and remain under military/government escort at all times during fuel discharge operations on the installation. 5. Sourcing Constraints, Compliance, and Industry Awareness Russian-Origin Fuel Prohibition: Russian-origin fuel or petroleum products sourced from Russian refineries, companies, or intermediaries are strictly prohibited without an explicit, formal statutory waiver. Proposed supply chains must guarantee and document full chain-of-custody traceability. Host Nation (KSA) Authority to Operate and Tax Exemption: Contractors must possess valid commercial registrations, transportation permits, hazardous materials (HAZMAT) transport licenses, and environmental authorizations issued by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Active Vibration Isolation System compatible with a Thermo Fisher Scientific Verios 5 Ultra High Resolution Scanning Electron Microscope (UHR-SEM)
description: The High Temperature Materials Group in the Structures and Materials Performance Laboratory of the National Research Council’s (NRC) Aerospace (AERO-SMPL-HTM) requires an active vibration isolation (AVI) system to achieve the required performance of the group’s ultra-high resolution scanning electron microscope (UHR-SEM). AERO-SMPL-HTM uses its UHR-SEM in advanced research on a wide range of materials for various applications. However, the instrument cannot provide the highest possible image resolution due to significant low-frequency disturbances during high-magnification imaging. A new AVI system will effectively dampen mechanical vibrations and eliminate disruptive low-frequency vibration noise that interferes with image acquisition. The new system will allow the UHR-SEM to achieve its optimum performance, and enhance AERO-SMPL’s capability to conduct advanced research and provide data for a large number of the research projects.

title: Economic Impacts of Rail Decarbonization in Canada
description: Title: Economic Impacts of Rail Decarbonization in Canada Solicitation Number: 5000096225 GSIN: B101 UNSPSC: 77101500 Description: 1. Summary 1.1 Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a study on Economic Impacts of Rail Decarbonization in Canada to Environment and Climate Change Canada. 1.2 The period of the Contract is from date of Contract to 2027-March-31 inclusive. 1.3 Offerors must submit their financial offer in accordance with the “Annex Basis of Payment”. 1.4 The mandatory and point rated technical criteria are described in the “Annex Technical Criteria”. 1.5 The Basis of Selection is Highest Combined Rating of Technical Merit (70%) and Price (30%). 1.6 The maximum funding available for the resulting contract is $70,000.00 (applicable taxes extra). Canada will declare offers valued above this amount as non-compliant. The Offeror acknowledges that this disclosure does not commit Canada to pay the maximum funding available. 2. Net-Zero Challenge Offerors of Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge. The Net Zero Challenge is a national initiative, led by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), that supports businesses in developing and implementing effective strategies and plans to reduce GHG emissions in facilities and operations to net-zero by 2050. The Net Zero Challenge aligns with Canada's obligations under the Paris Agreement to combat climate change and support Canada's Climate Competitiveness Strategy, which is building a prosperous net-zero future in which Canadian business and industry are well positioned to compete and lead in a global low-carbon economy. Currently, there is a mandatory federal requirement for high-dollar-value procurements. Moving forward, all offerors are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge regardless of the dollar value of the procurement. Offerors who join the Net-Zero Challenge are encouraged to: a. Measure and disclose their greenhouse gas emissions; and b. Commit to planning, setting, and achieving science-based GHG reduction targets aligned with the objectives of the Paris Agreement. Participation in the Net-Zero Challenge not only supports global climate goals but also benefits businesses by positioning them as leaders in a global low-carbon economy. For more information on how to join, please consult the Net-Zero Challenge page. 3. Security There are no security requirements associated with this solicitation. 4. Compliance with Code of Conduct The Offeror must comply with Canada's Code of Conduct for Procurement 5. Integrity Provisions Offerors must submit certain information for contracts subject to the Ineligibility and Suspension Policy (the policy) at the bid or offer stage. Offerors also have an ongoing obligation to update the Office of Supplier Integrity and Compliance if their information changes. Information to submit with a bid or offer and update as required - Canada.ca 6. Anti-forced Labour Requirements The Offeror states that the Work is not mined, manufactured, or produced wholly or in part by forced labour. In performing the Contract and regardless of who acts as an importer, the Offeror must not, directly or indirectly, deliver Work if it is mined, manufactured, or produced wholly or in part by forced labour. 7. Buy Canadian Policy The Government of Canada has introduced new policies to protect, build, and transform Canadian industries. Check out Buy Canadian Policy for more information on what this could mean for you. 8. Social Procurement Environment and Climate Change Canada supports the Government of Canada’s social and economic objectives, including increasing the participation of businesses from underrepresented groups in government procurement opportunities. As such, offerors owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities, are encouraged to submit a bid for this opportunity. 9. Certification Requirements Contracts with former public servants (FPS) in receipt of a pension or a lump-sum payment must withstand the closest public scrutiny and reflect fairness in the spending of public funds. To comply with Treasury Board policies and directives on contracts with FPS, Offerors must provide the information detailed in the bid solicitation certification component. 10. Debriefings Offerors may request a debriefing and feedback on their results of the bid solicitation process. Offerors should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 11. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Offerors may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 12. Additional Information For additional information, interested offerors must contact the Contracting Officer named in this Notice.

Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than two (2) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: APN - Housing Construction Plan
description: Advance Procurement Notice Housing Construction plan Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. This is an advance notice for potential contracts to provide interested Design-Builders an opportunity to learn about the upcoming housing construction program. Note that there is no guarantee that these solicitations will proceed. Description of the Program and Services The Canadian Forces Housing Agency (CFHA) is planning a Housing Program to support the delivery of new residential housing for members of the Canadian Armed Forces at bases and wings across Canada. CFHA is responsible for the provision and management of military housing on Department of National Defence (DND) lands, and this program supports ongoing efforts to modernize and expand the housing portfolio to meet current and future operational needs. The objective of the program is to deliver new housing efficiently and at speed through Modified Design -Build (MDB) delivery model that integrates studies, design and construction under a single contract. The services required under this program include: Architectural & Engineering (A&E) services for the provision site studies, planning and detailed design development and all associated works. Design and construction of new infrastructure and housing to support the residential housing program. Note that certain locations may involve phased delivery. Planned building types will emphasize higher-density development, primarily mid-rise apartment buildings. The proposed number of units at each location is subject to adjustment as requirements are finalized. It is anticipated that each location will be delivered under its own Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. However, subject to change, certain locations may be bundled and procured through a single Request for Proposals (RFP), as outlined below in no particular order. It is anticipated that Indigenous communities will benefit from potential subcontracting, employment, and training opportunities arising from this program of work. title: Snow removal and de-icing services for AAFC's Kentville RDC
description: Snow removal and de-icing services for Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada’s (AAFC) Kentville Research and Development Centre (KRDC). To ensure all vehicular and pedestrian traffic areas remain safe, accessible, and free of snow and ice during the contract period. The Contractor will be required to perform snow removal and de-icing during the non-busy occupational period of the KRDC as well as on demand services, as when and if required by the Project Authority.

title: Collaborative Furniture Lease
description: This Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is issued to notify suppliers of the intent of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada (HICC) to enter into a contract with Advanced Business Interiors for the provision of a collaborative furniture leasing solution, as permitted under applicable procurement policies and trade agreements. An ACAN allows other suppliers to demonstrate their capability to fulfill the requirements. If no other supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements on or before the closing date, HICC may proceed with the award to the identified supplier.

title: Snowmobile and ATV Delivery and Rental
description: The Department of National Defence has a requirement for the provision of short term All Terrain Vehicle (ATC) and Snowmobile Vehicles rentals for the dates starting 11 Jan 2027 ending 29 Jan 2027 (SAR Tech Land Survival Training) and starting 9 Aug 2027 to 12 Aug 2027 (SAR Ground Ops Operation).

title: Tube,Metallic
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence has a requirement for the items detailed below. The delivery is requested at CFB Halifax, Nova Scotia and CFB Esquimalt, British Columbia. Line Item 1, TUBE, METALLIC Part Number: 140143 GSIN: 4710 NCAGE: 00945 Manufacturer: ALCO INVESTMENT COMPANY Quantity: 30, Unit of Issue: FT, to be delivered to CFB Halifax, Nova Scotia. Line Item 2, TUBE, METALLIC Part Number: 140143 GSIN: 4710 NCAGE: 00945 Manufacturer: ALCO INVESTMENT COMPANY Quantity: 30, Unit of Issue: FT, to be delivered to CFB Esquimalt, British Columbia. The requirement is subject to a preference for Canadian goods and/or services. All instructions, clauses and conditions are identified in the solicitation of offers by number, date and title. Offerors who submit an offer agree to be bound by the instructions, clauses and conditions of the solicitation of offers and accept the clauses and conditions of the resulting contract. Additional information on the solicitation of offers and the requirements of the solicitation will be attached as the Annex Statement of Requirements (SOR). Offerors must complete and submit the following in their original formats, Annex Offeror Submission Details (must be submitted in both the original Excel format and in PDF format), Annex Offeror Submission Form (PDF) Annex Offeror Declaration Form (PDF). Bidders proposing an Equivalent or a Substitute Product must indicate the brand name and model and/or Part Number and the NCAGE they are offering. The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Bids will be assessed on a Delivery Duty Paid (DDP) basis.

title: Clarke-Hess 5600 Phase Standard
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence has a requirement for the item detailed below. The delivery is requested at Edmonton, Alberta, by January 29, 2027. Item 1: Clarke-Hess Phase Standard Part No.: 5600 Quantity: two (2) Unit of Issue: EA To be delivered to : 7 CFSD Edmonton Receipts section, Bldg 236 East End 195 Ave & 82nd st. title: Recon Pro Field Kit V3
description: This notice is published on Buyandsell for a period of 15 calendar days. The Department of National Defence requires the following items: Recon Pro Field Kit V3 Each item must come with a Certificate of Calibration that is dated no more than 90 days before delivery date Requested delivery date for all of the above-mentioned goods is January 15th, 2027.

title: W684Q-253009 - Hazardous Gas Detection
description: Regional Individual Standing Offer (RISO) for hazardous gas detection system maintenance services for the Department of National Defence, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Esquimalt in Victoria, British Columbia Canada in accordance with the requirements detailed herein.

title: E6MON-260004-2 Standing offer for bulk road salt
description: PWGSC,on behalf of Federal Departments and Agency, is issuing this Regional Master Standing Offer (RMSO) for the acquisition of bulk road salt including delivery for Montreal Metropolitan Community located in Quebec, as detailed in Annex Statement of requirement.

title: EJ196-261312 - Maintenance Services Fire Protection and Life Safety Systems - Block 3
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and CanadaBuys posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by October 15, 2026 at 14:00. All bids submitted after 14:00 will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. Canada is seeking offers to provide maintenance services for the fire alarm, fire protection, and life safety systems to ensure their integrity and uninterrupted performance at Block 3 (Sir A John MacDonald Building, Booth Building, Dover-Brouse-Slater Building, Wellington Building and National Press Building). A mandatory site visit will be held on September 17, 2026 at 10:00AM. Offerors must communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than September 10, 2026 at 11:00AM to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) and date of birth(s) of the person(s) who will attend.

title: Installation of a Permeable Reactive Barrier at 335 River Road, Ottawa
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This requirement is open only to those Supply Arrangement (SA) Holders under EQ447-222370. This project is to provide construction services involving the remediation of 335 River Road impacted groundwater. Work is to be completed within 16 weeks after contract award. ENQUIRIES: Enquiries and other communications regarding the bid solicitation must be directed only to the Contracting Authority identified in the bid solicitation through the “Event Messages” tab within CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba). Failure to comply with this requirement may result in the bid being declared non-responsive.

title: RFI National Satellite Training Facility
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is requesting Industry’s feedback on a Request for Information (RFI) in advance of a Request for Proposal (RFP) pertaining to Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requirement’s for the National Satellite Training Facility. The purpose of this RFI is to: a. inform industry of CSC’s potential requirement; b. seek feedback on industry best practices; and c. provide industry with an opportunity to assess and comment on specific questions.

title: EE517-270245-2 - Cylindrical fenders for Base-Côte-Nord
description: PWGSC, on behalf of Transport Canada, is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) for the acquisition of cylindrical rubber fenders, including delivery, as detailed in Annex Statement of Requirement. Delivery point: Kégaska Commercial Wharf (Québec), G0G 1S0.

title: W7701-268094 Software development, modelling and simulation
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) on behalf of Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC), is issuing this Solicitation of Offers for the acquisition of specialized modelling, simulation and software development services in support of research, development, analysis and evaluation of military systems and capabilities located in Valcartier Research Center (VRC), as detailed in the Annex Statement of Work.

title: EE517-270528 Replacement of the cathodic protection system wharf 11 Cap-aux-Meules
description: Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), on behalf of Transport Canada is issuing this request for proposal (RFP) for the Replacement of the cathodic protection system wharf 11 Cap-aux-Meules. All details related to the requirement are found in the solicitation.

title: EC016-270565-B - ITQ - Fire Alarm System Replacement - St. John’s, NL Commun
description: Reissue of Solicitation of Offers. EC016-270565-B - ITQ - Fire Alarm System Replacement - St. John’s CCC, NL Work of this Contract comprises of the complete replacement of the facility’s fire alarm system within the Community Correctional Centre building in St. John’s, NFLD. This is the first phase of a 2 phase process: the first phase will evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers; the second phase will invite the qualified suppliers to provide a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. The qualification list will expire within 60 days or upon award of a contract in Phase 2, whichever is earlier, and the prequalification list will not be used in any other solicitation. This solicitation of offers is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of notification that their bid was unsuccessful. Reference the solicitation for further details.

title: 23135-270254_Enclosed trailer
description: PWGSC, on behalf of Natural Resources Canada, is issuing this request for proposal (RFP) for the acquisition of an enclosed trailer including delivery in Quebec City, as detailed in Annex “Statement of Requirements”.

title: W168A-26MK06-GYM EQUIPMENT
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and CanadaBuys posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by October 15, 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT. All bids submitted after 2:00 PM EDT will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. Canada is seeking offers from offerors to provide, deliver, and assemble commercial gym equipment with flooring to Department of National Defence.

title: B8114-270012 Furniture Modernization - Sydney, NS
description: This NPP is issued pursuant to PWGSC Supply Arrangement (SA) # E60PQ-140003/D and covers a requirement from the following product category (ies) of the SA: - Product Category 1 - Workstation Systems; - Product Category 2 Work Surface Products; - Product Category 3 - Filing and Storage Products; - Product Category 5 Ancillary Products; - Product Category 6 – Collaborative Products; - This requirement also contains products that are NON-SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT. Immigration Refugees and Citizenship Canada, has a requirement for the purchase, delivery and installation of office furniture to Sydney, Nova Scotia, by April 1st, 2027. This NPP covers a requirement to be solicited amongst the General stream of Suppliers (SA holders). Only suppliers who are pre-qualified and have been issued a supply arrangement are eligible to bid. Non-Supply Arrangement (Non-SA) holders may submit a bid to the Identified User (IU) but must also submit an arrangement to the Supply Arrangement Authority (SAA) for evaluation. Canada is not required to delay the award of a resulting contract pending the evaluation of an arrangement and issuance of a SA by the PWGSC Supply Arrangement Authority. If you wish to find out how you can be a pre-qualified SA holder, please contact RCNAmeublement.NCRFurniture@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca

title: W0113 27CS28 Hydraulic Box and Pan
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. The Department of National Defense (DND) has a requirement for the supply and delivery of one new Hydraulic Box & Pan Brake at CFB Bordan, located in Bordan Ontario in accordance with the statement of requirement.

title: EB144-270796-Dredging and Containment Cell - Three Fathom Harbour
description: Class “B” Dredging of the harbour channel and containment cell construction for Three Fathom Harbour, Small Craft Harbours (SCH). The Contractor is responsible for transportation of dredge material to the newly constructed on site containment cell at Three Fathom Harbour

title: EB129-270316 Consultant Services for Fit-up Design (ESDC, Dartmouth, NS)
description: PSPC, on behalf of Employment and Social Development Canada, has a requirement for consultant services for an office space fit-up project for the Dartmouth Management Centre, Dartmouth, Nova Scotia. Debrief: Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of notification that their bid was unsuccessful. The RFP issuing office is: Atlantic Region Acquisitions, 1713 Bedford Row, Halifax, NS B3J 1T3. This office provides services in English. Proposals may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Reference the solicitation for further details.

title: PR25073 23240-270244 Ultrasonic Microwave Reaction System
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Ensure you are fully registered in CanadaBuys/SAP Ariba! Combined Ultrasonic Microwave Reaction System Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) has a requirement for one combined ultrasonic microwave reaction system. All deliverables to Ottawa, ON must be delivered within fifteen weeks of contract award. Interested suppliers must meet the mandatory requirements detailed in the Statement of Requirement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada.

title: 5P122-260125 Tracked Rubber Track Dumper
description: The response time deadline is 14:00 EST Parks Canada requires supply and delivery of one (1) Rubber Tracked Dumper before March 31 2027 to Kejimkujik National Park in Nova Scotia. This solicitation of offers is open only to Canadian suppliers. Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days from receipt of notification that their bid was unsuccessful. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Ensure you are fully registered in CanadaBuys/SAP Ariba!

title: Phase 1 EZ899-270648 Fuel Tank and Dispenser Replacement
description: Works associated with this project include, but are not limited to, the demolition of existing fuel tank(s) and the installation of new fuel tanks (including fuel dispenser and submersible turbine pumps) while preserving the existing Computrol Fuel Site Controller.

title: Phase 1 ITQ - EP922-270356 NRCan – Geological Survey of Canada (GSC) Generator Load Capacity
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. This requirement is Limited to Indigenous Offers. This is the first phase (Phase One) of a two-phase process: the first phase will evaluate the required Indigenous Eligibility Certification. The second phase (Phase Two) will invite the qualified offerors to submit a technical and financial bid. If the Offeror fails to provide the completed certification as part of its Offer, the Contracting Authority may, at its discretion, provide the Offeror with a deadline for submitting a completed copy of the certification. title: France – Mine warfare and auxiliary ships – Fourniture de drones navals de surface d’endurance embarqués, mis en œuvre depuis des bâtiments de la Marine Nationale, et réalisation de prestations associées
description: Le marché consiste à acquérir des drones d’endurance à des fins de recueil de renseignement et d’établissement de situation tactique au-dessus et en dessous de la surface. Les drones doivent être embarquables et mise en œuvre depuis des bâtiments de la Marine Nationale (par exemple de type PHA, BSAM), de jour comme de nuit. Le drone peut être appréhender comme une plateforme comportant, diverses charges utiles et un système C2 et doit être modulaire et évolutif. Il doit être livré avec les interfaces permettant son intégration au bâtiment porteur. Le drone doit avoir une élongation d’au moins 100 nq et une autonomie de 5 à 10 jours en fonction de sa mission. Il doit être capable de conduire sa mission jusqu’à mer 4 minimum. Il s’agit d’un marché composite (pouvant comporter, outre une partie forfaitaire, une partie à bons de commande et une partie provisionnelle). La quantité maximale de drones visée est de quelques dizaines.

title: Germany – Architectural services for buildings – BAL201001/2027 Dach- und energetische Sanierung Gebäude C und D, Philipp-Matthäus-Hahn-Schule
description: Die Planungsleistungen umfassen eine Dach- und energetische Sanierung der Philipp-Matthäus-Hahn-Schule in Balingen. Die zu sanierenden Gebäude C und D wurden in den Jahren 1978/1979 errichtet. Die beiden miteinander verbundenen Gebäude umfassen eine Nutzfläche von mehr als 6.000 m² und beherbergen überwiegend Werkstätten und Unterrichtsräume. Sie sind eingeschossig, nicht unterkellert und wurden in Massivbauweise mit Stahlbetontragwerk, Flachdächern und Sheddach-Elementen errichtet. Ein zweigeschossiger Holzlagerraum mit flach geneigtem Blechdach wurde 2005 an das Gebäude C angebaut. Die Baumaßnahme soll während des laufenden Schulbetriebs durchgeführt werden. Schmutz- und lärmintensive Arbeiten sind daher, soweit möglich, in die schulfreien Zeiten (z. B. Ferien oder unterrichtsfreie Nachmittage) zu legen. Die gesamte Aufgabenbeschreibung finden Sie in der Anlage 01 Verfahrensleitfaden. Die Fertigstellung und die Übergabe an die Schule sind spätestens für Dezember 2032 geplant.

title: Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – CEFTA Cloud Infrastructure, Hosting, Managed Services, Security and Business Continuity
description: Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the end-to-end operation, administration, monitoring, maintenance, security, backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services. This includes Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Oracle databases, WebLogic middleware components, cloud and software licences, security platforms and tools, hosting environments, and associated support arrangements. The services will ensure the stable, secure, resilient, and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT, and other related platforms and services. The contractor shall ensure the availability, confidentiality, integrity, and resilience of CEFTA’s infrastructure, systems, applications, and data, in line with industry best practices and applicable security, compliance, and governance requirements. The scope includes infrastructure and platform administration, performance monitoring and tuning, capacity planning, availability management, patch and configuration management, incident, problem, change and release management, and service request fulfilment. The contractor shall provide a combination of proactive and reactive operational support. Proactive services will include continuous monitoring, preventive maintenance, performance and capacity management, security assessments, vulnerability management, patching, security hardening, resilience improvements, cost optimisation, compliance support, and recommendations for continuous service enhancement. Reactive services will include incident response, troubleshooting, service restoration, problem resolution, emergency remediation activities, security incident handling, and support for unplanned events affecting the availability, performance, integrity, or security of CEFTA systems and services. The contract will also include security monitoring, threat detection, cybersecurity risk assessments, vulnerability remediation, backup management, disaster recovery planning and testing, business continuity planning and validation, data protection measures, recovery readiness activities, cloud cost management, infrastructure lifecycle management, operational reporting, service-level performance tracking, documentation maintenance, knowledge transfer, and technical and architectural advisory services, ensuring alignment with CEFTA’s operational, security, and strategic business objectives while maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and recoverability of CEFTA information assets and digital services.

description: Allgemein: Im Bauabschnitt 1 werden die Freiflächen zwischen Ostflügel des Schlosses und der Ilmböschung bearbeitet. Das Bearbeitungsgebiet reicht von der nördlichen Gebäudekante des Schlosses bis an die Sternbrücke und schließt dabei die Fläche zwischen dem Osteingang des Schlosses und der Sternbrücke mit ein. Die Fläche zwischen Osteingang Schloss und Sternbrücke erhält einen Natursteinpflasterbelag. Alle Erdarbeiten werden durch das TLDA/ Archäologische Denkmalpflege begleitet. Grobmengen: 1 St Baustelleneinrichtung 11 St Baumfällungen 9 St Baumschnittarbeiten 610 m2 Asphalt abbrechen 85 m2 Natursteinpflaster aufnehmen und lagern 1100 m3 Boden lösen, lagern 1100 m3 Bodenaushub entsorgen 160 m Kantenstein aus Naturstein 540 m2 Wassergebundene Wegedecke, inkl. Oberbau 530 m2 Natursteinpflasterdecke (Liefermaterial), inkl. Oberbau 85 m2 Natursteinpflasterdecke aus Bestandmaterial, inkl. Oberbau 285 m2 Pflanzarbeiten, inkl. Fertigstellungs-u. description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE � 36C26327Q0029 � DESCRIPTION AND INSTRUCTIONS Department of Veterans Affairs intends to issue a sole source award to GE Healthcare with Alpha Source Service Team for Bone Densitometry Training and Education. This award will be a purchase order for the equipment and under FAR Part 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. The NAICS code is 611710 and the size standard is $24 Million. The PSC is U009. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. The Government will consider responses received by the closing date of this notice. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct a full and open competitive acquisition or a small business set-aside competitive acquisition. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this announcement. If the Government decides to compete this requirement in the open market, a synopsis shall be issued utilizing the combined synopsis/solicitation procedure identified in FAR 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. A determination to not compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Description of the Requirement: Employees are to attend one (1) day of in-hospital training and education at the Iowa City VAMC provided by Probo Medical/Alpha Source Group, Inc. This training and education will allow Technologists to complete fully diagnostic and interpretable Bone Density/DEXA examinations on patients. Following completion, Technologists will have a complete understanding of the Bone Densitometry equipment and a thorough understanding of how to complete diagnostic Bone Density/DEXA exams. Equipment will be provided by the Iowa City Medical Imaging Department. Vendor will not have access to any of the systems. Documentation of the completed educational program will be provided to the Iowa City VAMC Medical Imaging Department. POTENTIAL SOURCES SHALL INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION IN THEIR RESPONSE: 1. title: SCARNG Regional Aviation Phase Support Center for AH-64E Aircraft Maintenance Support
description: This is not an invitation to submit offers or quotes. The South Carolina Army National Guard anticipates issuing a solicitation directly to at least three service providers and sources for the SCARNG Regional Aviation Phase Support Center regarding AH-64E maintenance support using the procedures outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.201-1. The intended set aside is an 8(a) small business set-aside. The intended NAICS is 488190 with the associated small business size standard is $40.0 Million, and the intended PSC is J016. Anticipated Award Date: On or before 04/14/2026. The National Guard Bureau, on behalf of the South Carolina Army National Guard (SCARNG), requires non-personal aviation maintenance services. The contractor shall perform Field and Sustainment Level maintenance support to include: Production control (PC), Quality Control (QC), Supply Management, scheduled / unscheduled maintenance, and repair of aircraft, as well as launch and recovery of aircraft prior to and after the conduct of flight activities. The contractor shall work in specialized shops associated with the Field level maintenance fixed base operations as well as perform troubleshooting and maintenance repairs on the flight line in support of the Army National Guard (ARNG). The contractor shall perform scheduled and unscheduled services, and corrosion control activities IAW government directives, policies, and technical publications on AH-64E aircraft. Services include Periodic Maintenance Inspections, modifications, correcting safety-of-flight conditions, and associated production control and administrative functions. All work will be performed on-site at the Army Aviation Support Facility #1 (AASF1), located at 1325 South Carolina Rd., Eastover, SC 29044. The Government anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation. The anticipated Period of Performance consists of a 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods, and one 6-month option to extend services in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. The contractor and its employee performing this service are required to have a secret security clearance. Anticipated Award Procedures: In accordance with RFO FAR 12.201-1(c)(2), the South Carolina Army National Guard intends to solicit quotations directly from at least three known competing companies and make an award to the quoter that represents the best value to the government at a fair and reasonable price. If interested in being sent a copy of the solicitation, please send an email to LTC Kevin Esber, Contracting Officer, at kevin.j.esber.mil@army.mil. However, the Government reserves the right to limit the contractors solicited to no fewer than three; therefore, including a capability statement and verification of contractor's secret security clearance is highly recommended. Requests to be included in the solicitation must be received by the Contracting Officer no later than Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 10:00AM Eastern Daylight Time. Best Value is anticipated to include Technical, Past Performance, and Price as will be defined in the Solicitation. This posting accomplishes the notice requirements required by RFO FAR 12.201-1 and RFO FAR 5.101. The point of contact for this notice is: LTC Kevin Esber at kevin.j.esber.mil@army.mil

title: Presolicitation Synopsis - Recycling Collection and Disposal - USAG-Rhineland Pfalz
description: The Contractor shall furnish all services, labor, parts, materials, equipment, tools and data (other than Government Furnished Property), necessary to provide recycling collection and disposal services for USAG RP Installations. Services include but are not limited to: Collection, transportation, segregation, storage and disposal of recyclable waste Supply, maintenance and service of both permanently placed and time-limited containers, bins and compactors of varying sizes for various types of recyclable materials Supply, maintenance and service of potable pedestals to facilitate the collection of recyclables Unique Requirements: Approximately 300 pick-ups/collection of various types of recyclables per month across various locations Lease, service and maintenance of approximately 150 collection bins, containers, and compactors of various types and 12 pedestal steps during period of performance Transportation and disposal of approximately 80 metric tons of various recyclables per month The proposed contractual action will be a Five (5) Year, Firm Fixed Unit Price (FFUP) Requirements type contract. These are commercial services and FAR Part 12 will be utilized. NOTE on SMALL BUSINESSES SET-ASIDE FAR Part 19.000(b)(1)(ii) states �Contracting officers may apply this part outside the United States and its outlying areas.� The contracting officer has determined that it is not in the best interests of the Army to use FAR Part 19 small business programs for this acquisition. In coming to this determination, the contracting officer considered that the contactor must be knowledgeable of, and comply with, local labor and other laws when performing these services in Germany. In light of this requirement, and given the availability of local sources, the contracting officer intends to solicit local sources as well as post the solicitation to SAM.gov. As such, there is no reasonable expectation that offers will be obtained from at least two responsible small business concerns IAW FAR Part 19.502-2(b)(1). Even if two small businesses offered to perform the requirement, the award would not reasonably be expected to be at fair market prices as required by FAR Part 19.502-2(b)(2) since the additional cost for a US-based small business to perform this requirement in Germany would likely be substantial. Further, the services required are routinely available such that award to a small business concern would not be in the interest of maintaining or mobilizing the Nation�s full productive capacity, war or national defense programs IAW FAR Part 19.502- 1(a)(1). title: Facilities & Furniture Support Services
description: Deadline: All submissions must be received no later than October 15, 2026. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal (ACC-RSA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 15.101(c) solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue one in the future. Solicitations are not available at this time. Any requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the United States Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the United States Government. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The information herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to pursue any course of action. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. The Government anticipates follow-on conversations may occur in the future. ACC-RSA is conducting market research on behalf of US Army Transformation and Training Command (T2COM), Combat Capabilities Development Command Aviation and Missile Center (DEVCOM AvMC) to ascertain the capabilities of interested parties outfitting US Government buildings and/or facilities for Redstone Arsenal. The Government will consider responses to this notice to assess industry interest and capabilities to inform its overall procurement strategy. A. The Government requires a contractor capable of delivering facility management, workspace planning and implementation, and relocations solutions for over 3,000,000 square feet throughout multiple buildings on Redstone Arsenal. B. This will also include workspace planning, interior design, change management, physical installation, and relocation logistics with furniture purchases occurring as incidental materials needed to perform the requirement. C. Some task orders may include the use of Computer Aided Drawings (CAD)-assisted design, space modeling, and may include breaking down, storing, transporting and reassembling specialized laboratory furniture and equipment. Telephone requests for additional information will not be honored. All responses are due via e-mail no later than 9:00 a.m. central time on October 15, 2026. Adobe PDF is the preferred format. Send RFI responses and any other capability documents to the following ACC-RSA points of contact: Samantha Keegan at Samantha.m.keegan.civ@army.mil and Tracie Marbury at tracie.a.marbury.civ@army.mil. All responses to this RFI must reference the current RFI number W31P4Q-26-RFI-FACL. Acknowledgement of receipt will only be issued if a return receipt is requested with submission. Please do not submit any classified information and clearly mark any proprietary data/information. All information submitted shall be adequately safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure. The Government reserves the right to request further clarification or request additional information to enhance the Government�s understanding of the respondents� submittal. Information submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned. Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with their capability statements that include responses to the following items. 1. Capability statements should have at least the following: a. Full Company Name b. Business Size (Large or Small) c. Small Business Certified Status, if applicable by the Small Business Administration. d. Point of Contacts: Names, Positions, Office and/or Mobile Telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses. e. CAGE Code. f. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). g. Whether you have an existing Government contract, Blanket Purchase Agreement, or a Multiple Award Schedule for these types of services and products. Provide associated contract, MAS and BPA numbers, if applicable. 2. Describe your experience as a prime or a sub, specifying which, with disassembling, relocating, and reassembling office and workstation furniture. 3. State whether your firm is an authorized, premier, or certified dealer for major commercial office furniture manufacturers with any or all the following: Steelcase, Haworth, MillerKnoll, and Indiana Furniture. 4. Provide the types of experience and certifications your organization possesses. If embedded in the capability statement submission, please restate in the response to this question. 5. Describe your in-house design capabilities. Indicate if you employ NCIDQ-certified designers or licensed space planners. 6. Describe any current supply chain risks and your strategies for mitigating delivery delays. 7. Describe your experience with the transfer of full commercial warranties (e.g., 10-year/lifetime) directly from the manufacturer to the Government, including managing factory recall or defect punch-lists. Include experience with managing multiple commercial warranties with different entities. 8. Indicate if your firm has an active facility clearance and the associated CAGE code. 9. Indicate whether any employees possess individual security clearances, status and current levels. 10. Describe any experience you have managing subcontractors. 11. Describe your approach if subcontracting work to, or teaming with another entity. 12. If you are primarily in the business of reselling and installing office furniture, describe how you would team or subcontract with another entity to manage aspects of the requirement with which you have no experience or expertise. 13. Which, if any, of the requirements in paragraphs A, B, or C would you need to subcontract? a. Indicate the approximate percentage (rounded to the nearest 10%) of labor your firm would perform without any subcontractors or teaming arrangements. b. Identify how you would address any challenges with teaming or subcontracting the requirement. 14. If this is a small business set-aside and you are responding as a Small Business under a Service NAICS, explain your methodology to satisfy 13 CFR � 125.6, requiring the prime contractor to self-perform at least 50% of direct personnel labor costs. Indicate if there are any challenges associated with performing at least 50% of the work. 15. Do you have a physical presence at or near Redstone Arsenal, AL? a. Detail if any extended commutes are applicable. b. What impact is there on the Government if a 24-hour suspense is desired? c. Include if there are any challenges associated with short suspense. 16. Indicate if you have any interest in attending an in-person meeting with the Government to further discuss our strategy, provide additional input, or ask additional questions.

title: USACE National Enterprise Dredging Center Scope Dredge to Budget Contract
description: Special Notice: W912PM27RA006 Title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget will occur on 16 October 2026 from 0900ET to 13:00ET via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing Scope Dredge to Budget acquisition strategy. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 15 October 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026. There will also be a face-to-face meeting with individual contractors that have the required equipment and intend to propose on this future solicitation. The face-to-face meetings will be on 03-04 November in Galveston, TX. Please respond to to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil of your interest in a face-to-face meeting no later than 24 September 2026 at 1PM ET.

Point of Contacts: Names, Positions, Office and/or Mobile Telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses. e. CAGE Code. f. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). g. Provide associated contract, MAS and BPA numbers, if applicable. 2. State whether your firm is an authorized, premier, or certified dealer for major commercial office furniture manufacturers with any or all the following: Steelcase, Haworth, MillerKnoll, and Indiana Furniture. 4. Describe any current supply chain risks and your strategies for mitigating delivery delays. 7. Include experience with managing multiple commercial warranties with different entities. 8. Indicate if your firm has an active facility clearance and the associated CAGE code. 9. Indicate whether any employees possess individual security clearances, status and current levels. 10. Describe any experience you have managing subcontractors. 11. Describe your approach if subcontracting work to, or teaming with another entity. 12. If you are primarily in the business of reselling and installing office furniture, describe how you would team or subcontract with another entity to manage aspects of the requirement with which you have no experience or expertise. 13. Identify how you would address any challenges with teaming or subcontracting the requirement. 14. Detail if any extended commutes are applicable. b. What impact is there on the Government if a 24-hour suspense is desired? c. Include if there are any challenges associated with short suspense. 16. title: Sepsis Research Blood Sample Collection Services
description: Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source Title: Sepsis Research Blood Sample Collection Services Requiring Activity: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR), Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch Related Notice: HT942523P0084 Product Service Code (PSC): AN11 - HEALTH R&D SERVICES; HEALTH CARE SERVICES; BASIC RESEARCH North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541714 - Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology) Small Business Size Standard: 1000 employees The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) on behalf of the Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch at the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR) intends to extend current contract services as a cost R&D contract on a sole source basis to Medstar Health Research Institute, Inc. (MHRI), 10980 Grantchester Way 7th Fl, Columbia, MD 21044-6097 USA; Cage Code 3J1M2 under the RFO FAR 6.103-1 � Only one responsible source can supply the required products due to the non-commercially available sources of the blood samples the Government is requesting. Description of Requirement: This is a requirement to extend and re-structure a Firm-Fixed Price contract into a Research and Development (R&D) cost type contract vehicle that will allow the Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch to procure samples from septic and non-septic burn patients along with longitudinal clinical data for the assessment of biomarkers of sepsis for refinement and validation of SeptiBurnAlert program. These blood samples; to include longitudinal clinical data, are currently being collected by MHRI in accordance with an approved Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocol and are actively recruiting subjects for patient samples that meet the specific thermally injured criteria. The Government will convert the current contract from a firm fixed price award to a cost type, RFO part 35 R&D contract to better align the requirement with the Government�s needs. This special notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Meaningful submissions received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. If no meaningful, written submissions are received by the date listed below, after the publication of this notice, the solicitation will be issued as a sole source requirement to Medstar Health Research Institute, Inc. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable vendor to fulfill this requirement is MHRI. Submit capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, or Excel attachments) to Ms. Nicole Applegate at e-mail: nicole.v.applegate.civ@health.mil Capability statements are due no later than 10:00am Eastern Time on October 15, 2026.

title: SCARNG Regional Aviation Phase Support Center for AH-64E Aircraft Maintenance Support
description: This is not an invitation to submit offers or quotes. The South Carolina Army National Guard anticipates issuing a solicitation directly to at least three service providers and sources for the SCARNG Regional Aviation Phase Support Center regarding AH-64E maintenance support using the procedures outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.201-1. The intended set aside is an 8(a) small business set-aside. The intended NAICS is 488190 with the associated small business size standard is $40.0 Million, and the intended PSC is J016. Anticipated Award Date: On or before 04/14/2027. The National Guard Bureau, on behalf of the South Carolina Army National Guard (SCARNG), requires non-personal aviation maintenance services. The contractor shall perform Field and Sustainment Level maintenance support to include: Production control (PC), Quality Control (QC), Supply Management, scheduled / unscheduled maintenance, and repair of aircraft, as well as launch and recovery of aircraft prior to and after the conduct of flight activities. The contractor shall work in specialized shops associated with the Field level maintenance fixed base operations as well as perform troubleshooting and maintenance repairs on the flight line in support of the Army National Guard (ARNG). The contractor shall perform scheduled and unscheduled services, and corrosion control activities IAW government directives, policies, and technical publications on AH-64E aircraft. Services include Periodic Maintenance Inspections, modifications, correcting safety-of-flight conditions, and associated production control and administrative functions. All work will be performed on-site at the Army Aviation Support Facility #1 (AASF1), located at 1325 South Carolina Rd., Eastover, SC 29044. The Government anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation. The anticipated Period of Performance consists of a 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods, and one 6-month option to extend services in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. The contractor and its employee performing this service are required to have a secret security clearance. Anticipated Award Procedures: In accordance with RFO FAR 12.201-1(c)(2), the South Carolina Army National Guard intends to solicit quotations directly from at least three known competing companies and make an award to the quoter that represents the best value to the government at a fair and reasonable price. If interested in being sent a copy of the solicitation, please send an email to LTC Kevin Esber, Contracting Officer, at kevin.j.esber.mil@army.mil. However, the Government reserves the right to limit the contractors solicited to no fewer than three; therefore, including a capability statement and verification of contractor's secret security clearance is highly recommended. Requests to be included in the solicitation must be received by the Contracting Officer no later than Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 10:00AM Eastern Daylight Time. Best Value is anticipated to include Technical, Past Performance, and Price as will be defined in the Solicitation. This posting accomplishes the notice requirements required by RFO FAR 12.201-1 and RFO FAR 5.101. The point of contact for this notice is: LTC Kevin Esber at kevin.j.esber.mil@army.mil

The scope includes associated HVAC modernization, architectural adjustments, electrical work, and plumbing tie-ins as detailed in the attached Statement of Work and project specifications for Project CTGB 13-2020. title: Interior redevelopment of the Arsenal Foundry – Québec Unit Field
description: 5P468-26-0177/A Interior redevelopment of the Arsenal Foundry – Québec Unit Field BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca . Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The Arsenal Foundry, located near Saint-Jean Gate in Old Québec, is a red-brick industrial building constructed between 1902 and 1906. Owned by Parks Canada, it is currently used as a museum space and as a venue for various rental events. In the fall of 2026, the interior structures currently installed within the building will be demolished to restore the building’s original interior volume and allow the redeployment of heritage machinery and exhibits on a single level. The demolition work will create an interior opening providing access to a lower level containing a nineteenth-century masonry remnant. This opening shall remain visible and accessible while being protected by code-compliant guardrails. Following this work, Parks Canada wishes to fit up the foundry to create a flexible, multi-purpose space intended for: 1 Heritage interpretation; 2 Permanent and temporary exhibitions; 3 Educational activities; 4 Corporate events; 5 Rental events. This mandate includes the design, supply and installation of new flooring finishes and guardrails under a turnkey delivery approach. Photographs of the building will be provided as an appendix to this Statement of Requirements. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $250,001 > $ 500,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SECTION 1: BID FORM AND CONTENT REQUIREMENTS. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than March 30, 2027. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT There will be a site visit on September 29, 2026 at 1:30 PM. Interested bidders are to meet at 2 D’auteuil street, Québec, QC, G1R 5C2. Bidders are requested to communicate with the Contracting Authority before the optional site visit to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders may be requested to sign an attendance sheet. Bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative will not be given an alternative appointment but they will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Germany – Engineering services – BAL201001/2027 Dach- und energetische Sanierung Gebäude C und D, Philipp-Matthäus-Hahn-Schule
description: Die Planungsleistungen umfassen eine Dach- und energetische Sanierung der Philipp-Matthäus-Hahn-Schule in Balingen. Die zu sanierenden Gebäude C und D wurden in den Jahren 1978/1979 errichtet. Die beiden miteinander verbundenen Gebäude umfassen eine Nutzfläche von mehr als 6.000 m² und beherbergen überwiegend Werkstätten und Unterrichtsräume. Sie sind eingeschossig, nicht unterkellert und wurden in Massivbauweise mit Stahlbetontragwerk, Flachdächern und Sheddach-Elementen errichtet. Ein zweigeschossiger Holzlagerraum mit flach geneigtem Blechdach wurde 2005 an das Gebäude C angebaut. Die Baumaßnahme soll während des laufenden Schulbetriebs durchgeführt werden. Schmutz- und lärmintensive Arbeiten sind daher, soweit möglich, in die schulfreien Zeiten (z. B. Ferien oder unterrichtsfreie Nachmittage) zu legen. Die gesamte Aufgabenbeschreibung finden Sie in der Anlage 01 Verfahrensleitfaden. Die Fertigstellung und die Übergabe an die Schule sind spätestens für Dezember 2032 geplant.
